commonSetting: Fix a probability space (Ω,mΩ,μ), μ a probability measure, and a filtration ℱ indexed by Nat. X,A,B,C are real processes strongly adapted to ℱ. Each X_n,B_n,C_n is integrable. A_n,B_n are nonnegative a.s. For each n, E[X_(n+1)|ℱ_n] ≤ (1+A_n)X_n−B_n+C_n a.s. A is summable a.s.; |C| is summable a.s. All series are finite real sums, not upper bounds admitting −∞. Separate countable a.s. statements may be combined only with the justified countability step. No integrability of A or of infinite error totals is assumed.

cases.sourceAssumptions: Fix a probability space (Ω,mΩ,μ), μ a probability measure, and a filtration ℱ indexed by Nat. X,A,B,C are real processes strongly adapted to ℱ. Each X_n,B_n,C_n is integrable. A_n,B_n are nonnegative a.s. For each n, E[X_(n+1)|ℱ_n] ≤ (1+A_n)X_n−B_n+C_n a.s. A is summable a.s.; |C| is summable a.s. All series are finite real sums, not upper bounds admitting −∞. Separate countable a.s. statements may be combined only with the justified countability step. No integrability of A or of infinite error totals is assumed. Fix deterministic real K ≥ 0 and assume X_n ≥ −K a.s. for all n.
cases.sourceConclusion: Almost surely B is summable and X converges to a finite real limit at least −K, allowed to depend on ω.
cases.proposedRoute: Direct application to X lacks hX0. Instead apply to Y_n=X_n+K with unchanged A,B,C; derive the drift and transfer the limit back.
cases.mathematicalJustification: Y≥0; E[Y_next|ℱ]≤(1+A)Y−B+C−KA≤(1+A)Y−B+C. Derive integrability/adaptation of Y and the conditional-expectation identity from source assumptions. No new integrability of A. The conclusion permits negative limits; it must not retain the original nonnegative-limit conclusion.

cases.sourceAssumptions: No source hypotheses. Proposed support is a theorem ∀ n : Nat, n=0 → n=1 → False. Separate supplied rows are rfl : (0:Nat)=0 and rfl : (1:Nat)=1.
cases.proposedRoute: Attempt a single theorem instantiation at one n; the separately valid rows at n=0 and n=1 cannot be combined.
cases.mathematicalJustification: The selected theorem is legitimate under inconsistent explicit premises; the source has no such premises. Do not import them, derive support from an added False, or infer that the selected theorem itself is false. This is a generic checking control, not stochastic evidence.

cases.sourceConclusion: There exists one deterministic real x such that almost surely X_n converges to x; B is summable a.s.
cases.proposedRoute: The retained theorem supplies a sample-dependent x. Direct premise coverage does not transfer the changed quantifier.
cases.mathematicalJustification: On Ω={0,1} with discrete sigma algebra, constant full filtration and probability 1/2 per atom, let X_n(ω)=ω and A=B=C=0. All original premises hold and each path is constant, but positive probability of each distinct limit precludes a common a.s. limit. Justify finite-space integrability, adaptation and uniqueness of real limits. The source realization must be checked, not replaced by a scalar formula.
